issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of the Frobenius inequality (part 2), the proof decomposes ker_c(ABC) = ker(BC) ⊕ M and ker_c(AB) = ker(B) ⊕ L and then treats x ↦ Cx as an injective operator M → L in order to conclude dim M = dim im(C) ≤ dim L. For x ∈ M one only gets (AB)(Cx) = ABCx = 0, i.e. Cx ∈ ker_c(AB); Cx need not be orthogonal to ker(B). Counterexample with H = F = R: A = [0 1] (1×2), B = [[1,0],[0,0]], C = [[0,1],[0,1]]. Then BC = 0, ker(BC) = span{e2}, ker_c(ABC) = F^2, so M = span{e2}; L = ker(B)^⊥ ∩ ker_c(AB) = span{e1}; and Ce2 = (1,1)^⊤ ∉ L. The dimension count dim M ≤ dim L is therefore unjustified as written.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the map M → L by the injective map M → ker_c(AB) (Cx ∈ ker_c(AB) since ABCx = 0) and observe C(M) ∩ ker(B) = {0}: if Cx ∈ ker B then BCx = 0, so x ∈ ker(BC) ∩ ker(BC)^⊥ = 0. Counting against the decomposition ker_c(AB) = ker(B) ⊕ L gives dim M ≤ dim ker_c(AB) − dim ker(B) = dim L, completing the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the Frobenius inequality (and, through it, Sylvester's inequality in part 3 of the same lemma and the rank equalities in part 3 of Lemma lemma:rank_properties) is unsupported; the inequalities themselves remain true, and the results that only use the inequality parts are unaffected.
issues.title: Proof of Frobenius inequality uses a map M -> L whose image need not lie in L
issues.why_classification: The standard two-line quotient argument repairs the single step; the Frobenius and Sylvester inequalities and all downstream claims (Lemma lemma:rank_properties, Lemma lemma:factorization_ranks, Corollary cor:added-1, Lemma lemma:cross_exists) survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $n_{\mathrm{rook}} = 0$, the rows are selected at random and the choice of columns is adaptive.

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm alg:rook_usual (and identically in alg:rook_bochner), j_* is initialized but i_* is assigned only inside the loop 'for s = 1, …, n_rook'. For n_rook = 0 the loop body never executes, so the declared output 'pivot indices (i_*, j_*)' contains an unassigned variable: the procedure has no defined input–output contract for this parameter value. The paper nevertheless runs its Stokes experiments with n_rook = 0 and asserts a specific behavior ('the rows are selected at random and the choice of columns is adaptive'), which neither rook block produces as specified; consequently the ABCD/ABCDX guarantees invoked in that configuration are not delivered by the specified procedures.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the boundary case well defined by a one-line fix: pass the starting row to rook and return the incoming pivot when n_rook = 0 (equivalently, initialize i_* before the loop), in both alg:rook_usual and alg:rook_bochner; all stated properties of ACA/ABCD/ABCDX then hold for every allowed input.
issues.overall_effect: The pivot-selection step is undefined for n_rook = 0, a value used in the numerical experiments; the output contract of the rook subroutine and, for that parameter value, the stated outputs of ABCD/ABCDX are not established.
issues.title: Rook-pivoting subroutine leaves the pivot row undefined for n_rook = 0
issues.why_classification: A single local boundary-case definition restores the input–output contract; the algorithms' guarantees on their stated domain and all reported conclusions are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In our experiment, we choose $\alpha_{\max} = \beta_{\max} = 2$, $m = n = 100$, and $K = 75$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the solution of eq:ode_bvp is the displayed sine series. Substituting u = (2/π)Σ u_k sin(kx) into −u'' − α²u produces Fourier coefficients (2/π)(k² − α²)u_k = (2/π)k(k²−α²)[1 − (−1)^k cos(βπ)]/[(k²+α²)(k²+β²)], whereas the sine coefficients of cos(βx) on (0,π) are (2/π)k[1 − (−1)^k cos(βπ)]/(k² − β²); these agree only at α = β = 0 (where the displayed formula is correct). The paper establishes no argument linking the displayed coefficients to the stated boundary-value problem, and with the equation as stated the operator −d²/dx² − α² has nontrivial kernel span{sin(αx)} at α ∈ ℕ, so for β ∉ 2ℤ the problem has no solution at the grid point α = 2 (α_max = 2 is used). The experiment therefore approximates a map that is not the solution map of eq:ode_bvp.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must make the equation and the coefficients consistent — e.g. flip the sign of the α² term in eq:ode_bvp (to −u'' + α²u) and replace (k²+β²) by (k²−β²) in u_k, or keep the equation, replace (k²+α²)(k²+β²) by (k²−α²)(k²−β²), and exclude the resonant parameter values from the grid; either fix preserves the qualitative experimental conclusions.
issues.overall_effect: The closed-form representation of the solution map of eq:ode_bvp is false, and for the stated equation the solution map does not exist on part of the sampled parameter grid; the reported comparison of ABCD, post-processed ABCD, random cross components, and HOSVD for this example is attached to a map that is not the solution map of the displayed problem.
issues.title: Closed-form coefficients of the model BVP do not solve the stated equation
issues.why_classification: The defect is repaired by a forced two-sign local correction (or by excluding resonant grid points); the algorithms, the comparison methodology, and every qualitative conclusion about the method survive unchanged, with no new lemma or construction.
